tldr: The population transport policies have equal marginal treatment-version shares, and their causal welfare contrast has a finite-energy scalar score. We now prove a data-only first-order precision bracket on the entire displayed class and match the parametric risk and finite-honest length rates for every \(d=2\), and for the explicit sufficient higher-dimensional region \(d(d+2\alpha)\le4(\alpha+1)^2\), \(d(d-2)\le4\min\{\alpha,\beta\}(\alpha+1)\). Strict inequalities give uniform full-score Gaussian inference and pointwise canonical efficiency at smooth strict-slack laws. The rough-regime sharp rates, necessary precision boundary, critical efficient limits and general envelope-boundary tangent projections remain open. Uniform canonical inference on the full class is impossible in every regularity regime.
